s1.syndrome_frame: Exertional dyspnea and syncope with abnormal cardiac findings
salient_findings: First-degree atrioventricular block with right bundle-branch block and left anterior fascicular block
key_facts: Dyspnea on exertion for the past year
Syncope during a bicycle ride with loss of consciousness for a few minutes
Elevated blood pressure of 150/78 mm Hg
Normal breath and heart sounds without any murmurs
Pulmonary hypertension (mean pulmonary arterial pressure 32 mm Hg)
First-degree atrioventricular block with right bundle-branch block and left anterior fascicular block
Third-degree AV block with minimum heart rate of 36 beats/min
Mobitz type I second-degree AV block with pause and junctional escape beat observed

shortlist.label: Lev-Lenègre disease
shortlist.why_kept: First-degree atrioventricular block and left anterior fascicular block are consistent with this condition

shortlist.label: Sick sinus syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Sinus rhythm with first-degree atrioventricular block and third-degree AV block suggest sinoatrial node dysfunction

shortlist.label: Cardiac amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Left atrial enlargement and uncertain diastolic function could be related to amyloid deposition

shortlist.label: Idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension
shortlist.why_kept: Pulmonary hypertension with mean pulmonary arterial pressure of 32 mm Hg is a key finding

shortlist.label: Atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Mobitz type I second-degree AV block with pause and junctional escape beat observed, suggesting AV nodal dysfunction

raw.rationale: The patient's ECG findings, including first-degree atrioventricular block, right bundle-branch block, and left anterior fascicular block, along with the progression to third-degree AV block, are consistent with Lev-Lenègre disease, which is a progressive cardiac conduction disorder often seen in older adults.

rejected.label: Sick sinus syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient has some findings suggestive of sick sinus syndrome, such as pauses and junctional escape beats, the primary issue appears to be with the AV conduction system rather than the sinoatrial node.

rejected.label: Cardiac amyloidosis
rejected.why: There is no direct evidence of amyloid deposition in the heart, and the echocardiogram does not show typical features of amyloidosis such as thickened ventricular walls.

rejected.label: Idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension
rejected.why: The patient has pulmonary hypertension, but it is not severe enough to be the primary cause of the patient's symptoms, and other cardiac findings are more prominent.

rejected.label: Atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia
rejected.why: The patient's ECG does not show evidence of supraventricular tachycardia, and the primary issue appears to be with the AV conduction system rather than reentrant tachycardia.
